options.label: Split: ratchet now, P6 residue later (Recommended)
options.description: P5 becomes its own backlog item outside RFC-0020: the size ratchet gate with override (no effect on run B, so no confound). P6 shrinks to one clause extending principle 9 to universal quantifiers at authoring time, filed now and landed after run B is scored. RFC-0020 gets a one-line pointer to both, nothing in its experiment changes. The rvw-pr paydown stays in the 'later RFC' bucket as recorded.

options.description: Add P5 and P6 to RFC-0020 anyway, overriding the 'Not in run B' exclusion and adding a confound with rule (c). Decision rule gains rows that n = 1 cannot score; I'd mark them 'observed, not decided'.

options.label: Ratchet only

options.label: File both, build nothing
options.description: Two backlog entries with dossiers carrying these verdicts; no RFC edit, no gate.

questions.question: `.claude/skills/`, `.claude/agents/` and `CLAUDE.md` match neither CODE_PAT nor DOCS_PAT, so a skill-only PR runs no gate job in CI today. How should the ratchet reach CI?

options.label: Add to DOCS_PAT (Recommended)
options.description: Extend ci.yml's DOCS_PAT with `^\.claude/(skills|agents)/|^CLAUDE\.md$` and wire the check into `docs-gate` + `preflight`. Skill-only PRs then run the docs job (incl. docs-build, a few minutes) — which also starts gating check-traces etc. on them. ci.yml edit ripples into HOOKS_PAT/tooling-tests.

options.label: Local only, bound stated
options.description: Wire into `preflight` (part of `hatch run all`, which /pr runs). No ci.yml change; the docstring states that CI never runs it on a skill-only PR. Cheapest, but bypassable.

options.label: Dedicated tiny CI job
options.description: New path-filtered job running only this script on `.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `sdd/` changes. Precise and fast, but adds a job against ADR-0043's job budget.

questions.question: When budgeted files shrink, what happens to the ceiling?

options.label: Must tighten (Recommended)
options.description: The check fails whenever the total differs from the recorded total by more than a small slack (e.g. 2%); shrinking requires `--update` to lock the lower ceiling in. A true ratchet: no hoarded credit, and every budget move is visible in the diff. Cost: an extra command after big cuts.

options.label: Credit allowed
options.description: Fails only above the ceiling; shrinking silently creates room that later growth can use up to the old peak. Lower friction, but 'net growth' is then measured against the last lock-in, not the previous commit.

When should the BK-422 ratchet merge, given run B?

options.label: Hold until run B scored (Recommended)
options.description: Finish it on this branch (tests, wiring, DOCS_PAT, backlog, trace, CHANGELOG), push, and leave it unmerged until RFC-0020's decision rule is applied. Run B's base and variant stay exactly as recorded; the ratchet's first raise then records whatever Phase 1 adds to ship/SKILL.md.

options.label: Merge before run B, variant raises
options.description: Merge now; rebase the variant and add a `--raise --item BK-418` to its commit. Run B then runs under the ratchet, which becomes a confound in RFC-0020 (like BK-414), and the variant no longer touches only ship/SKILL.md.

options.label: Pause here
options.description: Push what exists as a WIP commit (script, tests, budget) and stop; decide the rest after reading UNDERSTANDING.md on your PC.

Finding 2: cuts inside the 2% slack accumulate across merges and turn an unrelated PR red. Which remedy?

options.label: Keep slack, fix message + bound (Recommended)
options.description: Bound says in-slack cuts accumulate across merges and surface on a later PR; the shrink message adds 'if this PR made no cut, the cut is already on the base: run --update and commit the budget file'. Trimming PRs stay friction-free; the cost is an occasional one-command lock-in on someone else's PR.

options.label: Slack 0 on the shrink side
options.description: Any shrink fails until --update, so every trimming PR locks its own cut and nothing accumulates. Cost: every trimming PR rewrites total/files, so two concurrent trims always conflict on the JSON (the textual conflict your load() finding describes), and the slack bound/tests go away.
